requirements.title: A field is the record part processed for a data or character string edit descriptor
requirements.definition: A field is the part of a record read or written when format control encounters a data edit descriptor or character string edit descriptor; field width is its size in characters.

pending.data-edit-field-width: WRITE(buf,'(I3)') 7; expect '  7' and identify a three-character field.
pending.character-string-field-width: WRITE(buf,'("AB")'); expect 'AB' and identify a two-character field.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans use independent literal expected strings or scalar sentinels. Negative plans change one property from a conforming control and attribute the violation to this unit only.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Pending output plans prefer internal WRITE to a CHARACTER variable and name exact expected characters including blanks. Numbered syntax/constraint diagnostics are subject to 4.2 but need not assert a fixed diagnostic message, severity, status, or printed rule number. Unnumbered prose restrictions are not promoted to numbered-constraint diagnostics.

review_rationale: Independent fresh-context source review against the pinned J3/24-007 PDF, THREE ROUNDS: doc/source_audits/batch_136.json. This OPENS CLAUSE 13, previously unregistered. The reviewer re-read PDF p289-294, re-derived unit hashes rather than accepting the author receipt, and independently reconciled the accounting: the true movement is 2363 -> 2392, net +29, being 31 non-numbered units newly classified offset by two numbered deferrals. R1303 and C1302 were correctly left UNRESOLVED BUT ACCOUNTED because legacy fixtures already exist for them and registering a numbered rule with pre-existing cases structurally forces binding them, which a source packet must never do; a migration followup is recorded. Seven blocking findings were raised across three rounds and all closed: 13.4 p9 reversion was under-specified (nested-group target, no-preceding-parenthesis fallback, DT-parenthesis exclusion and the changeable-modes obligation were all missing); pending plans were placeholders rather than byte-exact specifications; 13.2.2 p2 was dispositioned permission despite carrying mandatory shall restrictions; C1309 omitted m, d and e. Two further defects were introduced BY the first correction and caught on re-verification: a plan that wrongly assumed record advancement for unlimited-item reversion, which Note 4 explicitly denies, and a negative that violated both p2 and p9 so could not isolate the rule it was filed under. The reviewer hand-verified all four exact record specifications against the source. Source accounting only: authored_facets unchanged at 1946, no fixture bound, no compiler invoked.
